title: job-post template variables
description: Values for templates/job-post.md.j2 and templates/job-post.html.j2. Generated by tpl-jinja from job-post.md; `description` on each property is the question put to the author.

engagement_length.title: Engagement length
engagement_length.description: How long this runs. Say it honestly - "ongoing" written to attract applicants for a two-week job is the fastest way to lose the contractor you wanted to keep.

industry_familiarity.title: Industry familiarity
industry_familiarity.description: The industry familiarity used under 'Nice to Have'.

outcome.title: Outcome
outcome.description: The problem you need solved or the outcome you need reached - not a list of tasks. "Our onboarding flow loses 60% of signups at step 3" attracts a different applicant than "design some screens".

rate_band.title: Rate band
rate_band.description: The rate range you will actually pay, with currency and unit. Posting without it triples your screening load and filters for people who negotiate rather than people who deliver.

role_title.title: Role title
role_title.description: The role as a contractor would search for it - "Figma UI designer", not "Design Ninja". This is the line that decides whether the right people ever see the post.

timezone_overlap.title: Timezone overlap
timezone_overlap.description: Required overlap with your working hours, stated as an offset and a window - "at least 2h overlap with UTC+2, 09:00-18:00". Timezone is the most common silent mismatch in contractor hiring.

weekly_hours.title: Weekly hours
weekly_hours.description: Hours per week you actually expect, as a range. Understating it to seem light is how a contractor discovers they took a half-time job and leaves in month two.
